title: NSPM-8: Winning the 6G Race
summary: NSPM-8 frames U.S. leadership in 6G communications as a national-security and economic priority. The memorandum connects next-generation networks with AI, robotics, spectrum, resilient communications, standards, supply chains, and grid or industrial operations.
key_findings: 6G is treated as foundational infrastructure for economic and national-security systems.
Standards, spectrum, research, security, and trusted supply chains are central implementation fields.
Future networks are linked to AI, autonomy, robotics, and critical operations.
why_it_matters: It identifies communications infrastructure and standards as dependencies for multiple frontier capabilities rather than as a standalone telecom issue.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking communications, compute, spectrum, standards, and equipment supply chains together.
Creates future watch questions for R&D programs, standards milestones, spectrum actions, and trusted equipment.
evidence_limits: 6G remains an emerging standards and research field rather than a deployed national network.
The memorandum does not establish performance, cost, coverage, equipment availability, or adoption.
